Subject: Privacy questionnaire — PII handling & transfer matrix

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this back. As part of our vendor risk review we need more granular answers to the privacy section of the questionnaire. High-level asks below — please include any supporting artifacts (DPA, subprocessors list, data flow diagram):

1) PII classification: for each product surface (API inference, embeddings, logs, telemetry) indicate what categories of PII may be processed, examples, and retention periods.
2) Data flow diagram(s): we need a labelled diagram showing ingress, processing, cache/KV, backups, and egress to any third parties (including monitoring, analytics).
3) Cross-border transfer matrix: what locations data may transit or be stored in; basis for transfer (SCCs, adequacy, explicit consent), and whether data for EU controllers can be constrained to EU-only residency.
4) Subprocessors: current list, purpose, location, and data access levels (admin, pseudonymized, cleartext).
5) Access controls & encryption: admin access policies, privileged access, BYOK/KMS options, and HSM integration.
6) Incident response & audit logs: how long audit logs are retained and how they are scoped by customer.

We are aiming to close the privacy review by 6/18. Can you provide the items above or propose a time to walk through? Attaching the portion of our questionnaire we still need answered (see attachment: privacy_section_needs.pdf).

Best,
Sarah Law
DPO, FinBank

--

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary of what we can share immediately and attachments included: Redwood answers to items 1–6 are in the attached 'pii-classification-table.csv' and 'finbank_dataflow_v2.png'. We've also attached a redline of our standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.pdf) and our current subprocessors catalog (subprocessors-catalog-060526.xlsx).

Short answers to call out:
- PII classification: API inference can carry user-supplied PII (names, emails, free-text identifiers) when customers submit such data. We mark these categories as "customer-controlled PII"; retention is configurable per-customer and defaults to 30 days for short-term KV/prefix caching, with 90 days for request logs used for billing/abuse prevention. Full details in the CSV.
- Data residency: We support EU-only residency for Enterprise customers via Redwood Private (VPC) and Dedicated region pinning. For hosted customers we route requests to EU regions where available; fallbacks to other regions can be configured by policy.
- Transfers & basis: We rely on Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for transfers from the EU to US for hosted customers; we can provide signed SCC templates and a UK Addendum if required.
- Subprocessors: the catalog lists subprocessors, their roles, and access levels; we include basic vetting metadata.
- Encryption & KMS: encryption at rest and in transit is standard; we offer customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated/Private deployments and HSM integration on request.
- Audit logs: we retain per-customer audit logs for 365 days by default; extended retention is available as an add-on.

Would it help to run a 30-minute walkthrough next week? We are available Tue 6/16 or Thu 6/18 (EU morning windows). If you prefer, we'll also upload a PDF with SCC text and the UK Addendum.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole

Hi Sarah — following up with the requested artifacts and next steps. Uploaded items to the shared Drive and attached a short transfer matrix PDF in the Drive folder. Key points below and next steps at bottom.

1) Regions & backups: Hosted (standard) — primary region chosen at account creation; logs and backups are stored in the same region by default. For EU controllers we persist backups and logs in EU regions unless the customer opts into a global failover policy. (See Drive: drive.google.com/redwood/finbank/region-backups-note)

2) Subprocessor access: see the new column in subprocessors-catalog-060526.xlsx (AccessLevel). Summary: monitoring/metrics vendors see aggregated telemetry only; analytics vendors may process pseudonymized payloads; CDN and caching partners may see request headers but not complete cleartext payloads except where required for edge inference (documented per-subprocessor). No subprocessors hold permanent copies of cleartext request data for hosted customers unless explicitly contracted and listed in the subprocessor row.

3) Transfer matrix: Drive contains a concise CSV mapping country -> processing/storage -> lawful basis (SCCs/adequacy/consent). For Hosted customers we use SCCs when data moves to non-adequate jurisdictions; for Dedicated/Private customers customers can opt for no cross-border replication.

4) Encryption & KMS: BYOK is available for Dedicated/Private; hosted customers can opt in to customer-managed keys in some regions (we've included the region list in the Drive doc). HSM-backed key storage is available as part of our enterprise HSM offering.

5) Audit logs & retention: default 365 days; on-request export and 24/7 read-only access for customers with Dedicated/Private plans.

Next steps / ask:
- I've uploaded the redlined DPA (finalized per our discussion) and prepared a DocuSign envelope. Please sign here: https://www.docusign.com/finbank/dpa-signature-link
- If you'd like a walkthrough, we can do Tue 6/16 at 09:00 CEST or Thu 6/18 at 11:00 CEST. Please confirm which works.

If you need a short summary paragraph we can add to the contract SOW to make retention and residency explicit — happy to do that.
